title: Local Model Residency
summary: See which local runtime holds each model and when it reloads
user: Privacy-conscious desktop users who run local models but need a plain explanation of model memory residency, unload/reload churn and which local client is consuming GPU/RAM.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Asks why ready-to-use offline desktop LLMs remain hard for ordinary users despite privacy and connectivity advantages.
Feature request says DBeaver Community lacks local-Ollama integration, showing sustained demand to keep AI-assisted workflows local instead of tied to a hosted tier.

recurrence: The 2026 audience request is for a ready working local experience; a separate local-runtime request shows technically capable users also prioritize local operation over hosted-only features.
current_workaround: Watch Activity Monitor/nvidia-smi, guess at keep-alive settings, or restart clients when a model becomes slow.
incumbents_and_gap: Ollama, LM Studio and Jan run models; system monitors show processes. The gap is a small vendor-neutral tray utility that translates runtime/model ownership and churn into actionable local diagnostics.
smallest_useful_product: Menu-bar/tray app that reads supported local-runtime status endpoints and OS process metrics, shows model load owner, GPU/RAM footprint, reload events and a safe copyable diagnostic bundle. Non-goals: model download, prompt logging, model serving, chat UI or cloud inference.
success_measure: In reproduced two-client tests, it attributes 90% of load/unload events to a process/runtime and users identify the reload source without opening a terminal.
monetization: free — broad runtime support and trust matter more than monetizing a diagnostic; paid enterprise adapters can follow.
constraints: No prompt/completion collection; query only documented local endpoints; disclose incomplete attribution; keep diagnostics local unless explicitly exported.
why_distinct: It makes local-model resource behavior understandable without becoming another model launcher or chat client.
